facts.text: Saint-Eustache's industrial hub north of Highway 640, including the Innoparc Albatros business district, provides 280 businesses and over 5,000 jobs.
facts.evidence: The industrial hub of Saint-Eustache is located north of Highway 640 and consists of an industrial park established in 1961 and a new innovative business district, Innoparc Albatros... provides 280 businesses and over 5,000 jobs.

facts.text: Nova Bus, a city transit bus manufacturer, is headquartered in Saint-Eustache in a former General Motors plant.
facts.evidence: Nova Bus is headquartered in Saint-Eustache, Quebec, Canada, and the Saint-Eustache factory is a former General Motors plant that built city transit buses.

facts.text: Sectors in the Saint-Eustache industrial hub include chemicals, automotive, metal products, IT and electronics, food and drinks, transportation and wood industries.
facts.evidence: The sectors of activity found there include chemical industries, automotive (manufacture, parts, accessories, auction), metals and metal product manufacturing, IT and electronics, non-metallic mineral products, food and drinks, transportation industries, and wood industries.

meta.descriptor: an off-island suburb northwest of Montreal on the Rivière du Chêne
meta.fact: home to Nova Bus headquarters and an industrial hub of 280 businesses and over 5,000 jobs

overview: Saint-Eustache had 45,276 residents in the 2021 Census, up 2.9 percent from 44,008 in 2016. That is steady, moderate growth for an established suburb northwest of Montreal, where most households are long-time residents rather than recent arrivals.

A large industrial hub, led by bus maker Nova Bus and automotive, metal and food firms, gives the city a solid local job base. Businesses here compete for practical, value-conscious households and for business customers in the industrial park, while larger chains along the highway draw shoppers from across the North Shore.
